text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan Muslim League's Liquat Ali Jatoi took oath as chief minister of Sindh province.
- The pharmaceutical industry in Pakistan has been allowed to increase the prices of locally manufactured medicines by four percent.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, after an attack on an Iranian cultural centre in Multan, said the date of his announced visit to Pakistan was not fixed.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has named President Farooq Leghari in the murder of her brother Murtaza Bhutto, saying the plan was "to kill one Bhutto to get another Bhutto."
- Two people were killed in apparently sectarian incidents of violence in Punjab province.
- Sardar Akhtar Mengal was inducted as the 13th Chief Minister of Balochistan province.
- The newly-elected Chief Minister of North West Frontier province Mehtab Ahmed Khan obtained a vote of confidence by securing 70 votes in the house of 80 members.
- The changing circumstances in India and Pakistan present an opportunity for a review of U.S. policy for the region, the U.S. State Department said.
- Foreign exchange reserves have increased to $870 million on Saturday from $700 million left by the caretaker government, said Sartaj Aziz, likely to be the next Finance Minister.
- The Iranian embassy in Islamabad has asked Pakistan to arrange complete security for its cultural centres, following an attack on its centre in Multan which left seven people dead.
- Indian external affairs minister I.K. Gujral has said that India was ready to discuss all thorny issues with Pakistan, including Kashmir.
- A South Korean team held preliminary discussions with Pakistan Railways officials to explore the possibilities of investment in rail links to connect Asia with Europe.
- Pakistan Oilseeds Development Board asked the government for a 500-million-rupee credit line to buy certified sunflower and canola seed in 1997/98 (July-June), an official said.
- South Korean Consul General Dr Moo Sam Chung hinted that in the changed environment of political and economic stability, Korean multinational companies would return to Pakistan.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Pakistan Steel has cut the price of billets by 600 rupees per tonne to make them economically viable, an official said.
- The business community has decided to lend a helping hand to the government's efforts for debt retirement by offering to deposit $1.0 billion from Karachi alone.

- Kyo Tae Kimi, Director Korea Trade Centre, said the Daewoo Corporation had approached the new government to discuss its project to set up a special industrial zone near Port Qasim with a total investment of $300 million.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
